create_category.description: Add a category to the catalogue. Give it a parent to nest it under an existing category, or a tree to put it at the top level - 'List categories' reports both for every category the store already has. Names are capped at 50 characters and categories can be nested eight deep.
create_category.name: create_category

parameters.description: The category's name, as shoppers see it. BigCommerce caps it at 50 characters.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The category to nest this one under. Leave blank and give a tree ID instead to create a top-level category.
parameters.name: parent_id

parameters.description: The tree to put a top-level category in. Read it from 'List categories' rather than assuming: it is 1 on most single-storefront stores but not guaranteed to be.
parameters.name: tree_id

parameters.description: The text shown at the top of the category's own page.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: Whether the category appears in the store's navigation and can be browsed.
parameters.name: is_visible

parameters.description: Where the category sits among its siblings. Lower comes first.
parameters.name: sort_order

parameters.description: The category's own web address, such as '/summer-sale/'. BigCommerce needs it to be unique: if it is already taken the category is still saved but keeps its generated address.
parameters.name: url_path

parameters.description: A publicly reachable image to show for the category. BigCommerce downloads it into the store.
parameters.name: image_url

parameters.description: How products are ordered on the category's own page.
parameters.name: default_product_sort

parameters.description: The title of the category's page, for search engines.
parameters.name: page_title

parameters.description: The summary search engines show under the page title.
parameters.name: meta_description

create_customer.name: create_customer

parameters.description: The customer's email address, which BigCommerce uses as their sign-in and requires to be unique across the store.
parameters.name: email

parameters.description: The customer's first name.
parameters.name: first_name

parameters.description: The customer's last name.
parameters.name: last_name

parameters.description: The company the customer buys for.
parameters.name: company

parameters.description: The customer's phone number.
parameters.name: phone

parameters.description: A private note about the customer, seen only in admin.
parameters.name: notes

parameters.description: The numeric ID of the customer group to put them in, which decides the pricing and discounts they see.
parameters.name: customer_group_id

parameters.description: The store's own code for this customer's tax exemption, if they have one.
parameters.name: tax_exempt_category

parameters.description: Whether BigCommerce may email the customer product review requests and abandoned cart reminders.
parameters.name: accepts_marketing

parameters.description: The first line of the customer's saved address. Needs the city and country below with it.
parameters.name: address_line_1

parameters.description: Apartment, suite or unit.
parameters.name: address_line_2

parameters.description: State, province or region on the saved address.

parameters.description: Postal or ZIP code on the saved address.

parameters.description: Country on the saved address, as a two-letter ISO 3166-1 code such as US, GB or DE.
parameters.name: country_code

parameters.description: A phone number for this address.
parameters.name: address_phone

parameters.description: Whether the address is a home or a business.
parameters.name: address_type

create_order.description: Place an order in the store for one catalogue product or one custom item, with a billing address and an optional status. Leave the customer blank for a guest order, which is what a checkout by someone without an account produces. The postcode is the only part of the address BigCommerce insists on.

parameters.description: The catalogue product to order. Leave blank to order a custom item instead, using the two fields below.
parameters.name: product_id

parameters.description: How many to order. One when left blank.
parameters.name: quantity

parameters.description: Order something that is not in the catalogue, by naming it here instead of giving a product ID.
parameters.name: item_name

parameters.description: What to charge for the custom item, per unit, as a plain number in the store's own currency. Required with a custom item, since BigCommerce has no price to look up.
parameters.name: item_price

parameters.description: Whose order this is. Leave blank to record it as a guest order.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: What state to create the order in. BigCommerce uses 'Incomplete' when left blank, which keeps the order out of the store's own order list until it is moved on.
parameters.name: status_id

parameters.description: The postal or ZIP code on the billing address. This is the one part of the address BigCommerce insists on, and it must be two characters or more.
parameters.name: billing_zip

parameters.description: First name on the billing address.
parameters.name: billing_first_name

parameters.description: Last name on the billing address.
parameters.name: billing_last_name

parameters.description: Company name on the billing address.
parameters.name: billing_company

parameters.description: Street address on the billing address.
parameters.name: billing_street_1

parameters.description: Apartment, suite or unit on the billing address.
parameters.name: billing_street_2

parameters.description: City on the billing address.
parameters.name: billing_city

parameters.description: State or province on the billing address.
parameters.name: billing_state

parameters.description: Country on the billing address, as a two-letter ISO 3166-1 code such as US, GB or DE.
parameters.name: billing_country_iso2

parameters.description: Email address on the billing address.
parameters.name: billing_email

parameters.description: Phone number on the billing address.
parameters.name: billing_phone

parameters.description: A note on the order, seen only in admin.
parameters.name: staff_notes

parameters.description: A note from the buyer, as left at checkout.
parameters.name: customer_message

create_product.description: Add a product to the catalogue: name, type and price, plus SKU, description, stock tracking and level, categories, brand, sale and retail prices, dimensions, barcodes and page metadata. The name and the SKU both have to be unique across the store.

delete_category.description: Remove one or more categories from the catalogue. Products filed under a deleted category are not deleted with it - they are left uncategorised. This cannot be undone, and at least one ID has to be named: BigCommerce takes these as a filter, so an empty one would not mean 'nothing'.
delete_category.name: delete_category

parameters.description: The categories to remove. Pick from the store's categories, or type their IDs.
parameters.name: category_ids

delete_customer.description: Remove one or more customer accounts and their saved addresses. Orders they placed stay in the store. This cannot be undone, and at least one ID has to be named: BigCommerce takes these as a filter and answers a filterless delete with a success that changed nothing.
delete_customer.name: delete_customer

parameters.description: The numeric IDs of the customers to remove. 'List customers' returns each as 'id'.
parameters.name: customer_ids

delete_product.description: Remove a product from the catalogue, along with its variants, images and options. BigCommerce has no trash and no restore, so this cannot be undone - hide a product instead by turning off 'Visible in the storefront' with 'Update product'. Orders that already include the product keep their own copy of it.
delete_product.name: delete_product

parameters.description: The numeric ID of the product to remove.
parameters.name: product_id

get_order.description: Read one order by its number: its status, every subtotal, tax, shipping and handling figure, the currency it was placed in, the payment method and status, the billing address, and the notes the buyer and staff left. Amounts come back as strings, which is how BigCommerce sends them.
get_order.name: get_order

parameters.description: The order's number. 'List orders' returns it as 'id', and it is the number shown against the order in Orders > View.
parameters.name: order_id

get_product.description: Read one product by its ID: name, description, SKU, every price, stock, dimensions, categories, brand, search identifiers and review totals - plus its images, variants, custom fields and options if you ask for them.

mock_response.meta_description: A 350ml stoneware mug, thrown and glazed by hand.
mock_response.name: Hand-thrown mug

get_store_information.description: The store's own settings: its name, domain, status, country and timezone, the currency and how amounts are formatted, the weight and dimension units the catalogue is measured in, the plan it is on, and its default channel.
